title: Project-distributions schema — grounded · constructed · derived
description: Machine-readable form of the project-distributions schema. The canonical prose spec is schema/SCHEMA.md and its illustrated companion is schema/schema-grounded.html; where they and this file differ, SCHEMA.md wins. A node states a `distribution` CONSTRUCTED from a shared corpus of grounded evidence; percentiles are a DERIVED readout (debug_computed_percentiles), never authored. Everything traces to a source. This describes the LOGICAL model; for the current run it is physically split — the shared corpus (documents/general_knowledge/speculations) lives in corpus/*.json and the nodes (keyed project::node) live in projects/*.json, one file per project. The prior run's single-file data is frozen under archive/calibration-run-1/.

documents.description: Shared corpus at the root: archived sources, each keyed by doc_<sha256[:12]>.

general_knowledge.description: Broadly-held reference-class priors, keyed by gk_<id>.

speculations.description: Stated-but-unsourced load-bearing guesses, keyed by spec_<id>.

document.description: An archived source and the home for its observations (I12: node → distribution → reference → observation → document).

sha256.description: content hash = identity; identical bytes are one record

core.description: lean, image-OCR'd text a reader opens instead of the raw file

derivation.description: present only if this document was computed from others (I13); every `from` id resolves

observation.description: One fact drawn from a document. Which nodes use it is derived on demand from projects/*.json (agentic-fetcher/citations.mjs), not stored — the stored cited_by cache drifted stale and was dropped (I11).

quote.description: verbatim sentence; may be null when read from a non-textual capture — then a capture_note says so and verification is not `verified` (I6)

capture_note.description: present only when quote is null: why there is no verbatim quote

verification.description: verified = non-empty quote present in core; unchecked = not yet swept; not_in_doc = swept, figure absent; unverifiable = real but not yet parseable (carries blocked_on)

blocked_on.description: present iff verification = unverifiable — what unblocks it (e.g. an OCR sidecar)

reasoning.description: why it is admissible without a single citation
why we lean on this un-sourced figure and what would confirm it

measure.description: The superstructure — only the parts the source states; never force-fit a p10/p50/p90 template (I10).

mean.description: arithmetic mean; grounds a splice tail's shape (§4.3)

points.description: named point-measures that are NOT probability quantiles (e.g. gaap/non-gaap margin, milestone shares, a voluntary/involuntary churn split) — one number per named label

series.description: a dated multi-point series; the operand extrapolate_cagr / extrapolate_linear consume

value.description: The recurring trail behind a grounded number (a param, an atom's/anchor's `at`, an input, a cross_check, a splice threshold).

value_type.description: open vocabulary, suggested below. computed_value carries a formula; direct_value (incl. a plain reference to a shared value) takes the number as-is.

reference.description: → obs_ / gk_ / spec_ / in_ by id; null = a counted gap (needs missing_document)

quantile.description: select one quantile (e.g. "p10") of the referenced measure's `quantiles` — for a value that restates one point of a stated distribution (e.g. a scaffolded anchor restating a speculation's authored quantile)

references.description: plural, when the value spans several grounded sources (I7)

formula.description: for a computed_value — ONE grammar over ids AND the distribution's own structure (segments[i], splices[i]), with the closed function set min/max/extrapolate_cagr/extrapolate_linear/slope_match (I22)

basis.description: metric-comparability marker; a metric/unit_of mismatch among a node's operands is flagged, never silently reconciled (I21)

allocation.description: The single mass-split decision on point_mass / weighted_combination.

atom.description: A point-mass atom: a value (the position, via its measure) plus a weight. The one allocation renormalizes the weights (I3).

value.description: optional nested position (else the atom itself is the value)

component.description: A nested distribution plus a weight (weighted_combination).

segment.description: A distribution governing one slice of the support (splice), ordered lower → upper.

splice_point.description: The transition between two consecutive segments. `at` is a position (or a mass fraction for a point-mass boundary), usually referencing a shared value the upper segment's location reuses.

anchor.description: A metalog anchor: an observed sample value (position via its measure; or a nested `value`). Its percentile is its rank i/(n+1), not authored. No weight.

value.description: optional nested value (else the anchor itself is the value)

distribution.description: kind IS the family. Structural: point_mass (atoms), weighted_combination (components), splice (segments+splices). Quantile-parameterized: metalog (anchors + k, optional lower_bound/zero_mass). Parametric families state named params as values. Exact per-kind keys: compiler/DESIGN.md. I2: complete for its kind.

lower_bound.description: metalog lower bound; null = unbounded (alias: boundedness + lower)

upper_bound.description: metalog upper bound; null = unbounded. With lower_bound, gives a doubly-bounded (log-odds) metalog for a fraction/rate whose tail must not cross a ceiling (alias: boundedness + upper)

zero_mass.description: metalog: probability mass sitting at lower_bound — the $0 free-tier hurdle

additionalProperties.description: a parametric kind's named params (median/sigma, alpha/beta, shape/rate, location/scale/shape, etc.), each a value

cross_check.description: A figure that corroborates or refutes the built distribution but anchors no part of it (I18).

superseded_by.description: present only on a refutation — the observation that replaced the disproven claim

node.description: The project-axis distribution the model consumes — an elicited leaf; holds no evidence of its own, only references into the corpus.

inputs.description: node-local named Values (I19: a DAG), keyed by in_<id>

truncation.description: optional — only bounds that actually clip beyond the distribution's natural domain (I16)

reconciliation.description: how multiple / conflicting sources were combined (P5)

support_score.description: how grounded the whole distribution is, overall

reasoning.description: the rationale for support_score — the node's one free-standing narrative

debug_computed_percentiles.description: percentiles/mean read off the distribution — throwaway, recomputable, never authored (I1)
